Stages.Title: Seed Selection
Stages.Description: Choosing the right hybrid and seed quality

Subsections.Heading: 1.1 Recommended Hybrids for Dharwad Region
Subsections.Text: Dharwad district in northern Karnataka receives moderate to heavy rainfall (700-900 mm) during Kharif. The following hybrids are well-suited to local agroclimatic conditions, combining high yield potential, disease tolerance, and standability.

Subsections.Heading: 1.3 Seed Treatment Protocol
Subsections.Text: Seed treatment is essential to prevent soil-borne fungal diseases, damping-off, and to promote uniform germination. Follow the sequence below strictly.
Important Notes: Apply biological agents (Trichoderma, Azospirillum) LAST, always after chemical treatments.
Never mix Trichoderma directly with chemical fungicides in the same step.
Use treated seed within 24 hours. Do NOT store treated seed.

Table.Action (THEN): REJECT seed lot procure certified seed from authorised dealer
Dry seed in shade for 2-3 days, retest before treatment
Use Imidacloprid 70 WS @ 5 ml/kg seed as mandatory treatment
Treat with Metalaxyl-M 350 FS @ 6 ml/kg seed additionally

Stages.Title: Land Preparation
Stages.Description: Soil testing, tillage, and basal organic matter

Subsections.Heading: 2.1 Soil Suitability for Dharwad
Subsections.Text: Maize thrives in well-drained, deep loamy soils. Dharwad district predominantly has medium-black (vertisol) and red lateritic soils. Both are suitable for maize with appropriate management. Waterlogging must be avoided at all costs.

Table.Action (THEN): Apply agricultural lime @ 2-4 q/acre; wait 6-8 weeks before sowing
Apply gypsum @ 1-2 q/acre; ensure good drainage
Deep plough to break hard pan; ensure proper drainage channels
Use subsoiler at 35-40 cm depth before normal tillage
Apply FYM 5 tons + Vermicompost 1 ton/acre mandatorily
Apply Carbofuran 3G @ 8 kg/acre or Neem cake @ 150 kg/acre in furrows

Stages.Title: Vegetative Stage (15-45 DAS)
Stages.Description: Nitrogen management, weed control & crop protection

Subsections.Heading: 5.1 Recommended Fertiliser Schedule - Dharwad
Subsections.Text: The total fertiliser recommendation for maize in Dharwad district (medium black soils) is 120:60:40 kg NPK/ha (approx. 48:24:16 kg/acre). Nitrogen is split to improve use efficiency and reduce losses.

Table.Dose / Acre: 40 kg DAP + 25 kg MOP + 10 kg ZnSO4

Best Practices: Apply urea as band placement 5-7 cm from plant base and immediately cover with soil.
Never broadcast urea before rain ammonia volatilisation loss can reach 40-60%.
If irrigation available, apply urea and irrigate within 24 hours.
Fertigated urea through drip gives 30-35% higher N-use efficiency.

Table.Irrigation if No Rain: One irrigation if soil moisture <50% FC

Subsections.Heading: 5.4 Fall Armyworm (FAW) Management - Spodoptera frugiperda
Subsections.Text: FAW is the most critical pest of maize in Karnataka. Monitor whorls for feeding damage. Early detection (V3-V6) is crucial for effective management.

Table.Action (THEN): Apply 1st urea top dressing @30 kg/acre band placement
Apply 2nd urea @ 15 kg/acre + earthing-up operation
Nitrogen deficiency apply urea foliar spray 2% or soil application
Zinc deficiency - spray ZnSO4 0.5% twice at 7-day interval
Apply Emamectin Benzoate 4 g/15L or Chlorpyrifos 2 ml/L in whorl
Manual weeding + inter-cultivation immediately
Irrigate @ 3-4 cm; maize at V6 is sensitive to moisture stress

Stages.Title: Tasseling (45-65 DAS)
Stages.Description: Irrigation priority, pollination protection & nutrient management

Subsections.Heading: 6.1 Tasseling Stage Overview
Subsections.Text: Tasseling marks the beginning of the reproductive phase. The tassel at the top of the plant sheds pollen over 5-8 days. Any moisture stress during this period severely reduces pollination and cob set. This is the FIRST CRITICAL IRRIGATION PERIOD.

Table.Value / Recommendation: Furrow/sprinkler preferred; avoid overhead wetting at pollen shedding time
50-70% relative humidity optimal for pollen viability
Tassel tip visible at top of plant irrigation due immediately

Table.Visual Symptom: Leaf rolling, grey-green colour, tassel delayed
Yellow V from leaf tip, weak tassel
Pollen not shed / shed early (morning only)
Frass in tassel, feeding on pollen

Table.Action (THEN): IRRIGATION PRIORITY = HIGH - irrigate within 48 hours

Table.Condition (IF): No rain for 10+ days during tasseling
Table.Action (THEN): Irrigate immediately @ 4-5 cm; repeat every 6 days
Emergency irrigation required direct impact on cob count
Irrigation cools canopy; schedule irrigation in late afternoon
Severe water stress irrigate within 24 hours
Ensure drainage; check for Maydis Blight if humid
Cannot be corrected this is a forecast warning only; prevent by irrigation

Stages.Title: Silking (65-75 DAS)
Stages.Description: THE MOST CRITICAL STAGE - zero tolerance for moisture stress

Subsections.Heading: CRITICAL STAGE ALERT
Subsections.Text: Silking is the single most yield-determining stage in maize. Even 1-2 days of moisture stress at silking can cause 50-70% yield loss. Every silk must receive pollen for a kernel to form stress prevents silk emergence. Monitor daily during this 10-day window. Do NOT miss irrigation timing.

Table.Value / Recommendation: Fine, pale-green, thread-like silks emerge from husk tip
Tassel sheds 2-3 days before silk; synchrony critical
100-120 mm highest of entire crop duration
Every 5-6 days; do NOT allow any wilting
5-8 days; fertilisation occurs 24 hrs after pollen lands
Set at this stage determines final cob weight

Subsections.Heading: 7.2 Silk Synchrony & Pollination Management
Subsections.Text: Poor synchrony between tasseling and silking is a major yield constraint. Silks that emerge after pollen shed ends are not fertilised. Management options are limited at this stage prevention via timely sowing is the best strategy.

Table.Action (THEN): IRRIGATION PRIORITY = VERY HIGH - irrigate same day if soil dry
YIELD LOSS RISK = VERY HIGH - irrigate immediately, every 5 days
Irrigation + potassium spray (0.5% K2SO4) to reduce heat stress

Table.Condition (IF): Silk browning before full cob fill
Table.Action (THEN): Premature drying indicator of severe stress; assess yield loss
Emergency irrigation within 12 hours critical yield window

Table.Condition (IF): Rain > 60 mm in 3 days during silking
Table.Action (THEN): Check drainage; apply propiconazole for fungal disease control

Table.Condition (IF): FAW damage on cob entry point
Table.Action (THEN): Apply Emamectin Benzoate 4 g/15L into silk channel

Stages.Title: Grain Filling (75-105 DAS)
Stages.Description: Carcohydinte accumulation potassium role & imigation schedule

Table.Key Process: Rapid cell division; kernel number set
Rapid dry weight gain in grain

Subsections.Heading: 8.2 Potassium's Critical Role in Grain Filling
Subsections.Text: Potassium (K) is the most important nutrient during grain filling. It regulates stomatal function, reduces water loss, and drives sucrose translocation from leaves to grain. Potassium deficiency at this stage causes poor grain weight and shrivelled kernels.

Table.Agronomic Impact: Reduces ear rot and stalk rot incidence
Better grain quality and protein content

Application Details: If soil K is LOW: Foliar spray -0.5-1.0% K2SO4 (Potassium Sulphate) at R1-R3 stage.
Apply foliar K in cool hours (early morning or late evening) to avoid leaf burn.
Soil MOP application: If not applied at basal, apply 20-25 kg MOP/acre before R2.
Foliar K improves grain weight by 8-15% in K-deficient soils (ICAR trials, Karnataka).

Table.Action (THEN): Apply foliar K2SO4 0.5%; ensure irrigation every 7-8 days
Provide mechanical support if possible; check for stalk rot
Apply MOP 25 kg/acre soil application OR foliar K2SO4 spray

Table.Condition (IF): No rain for 12+ days at dough
Table.Action (THEN): Irrigate withholding at R4 reduces grain weight 8-12%
Set traps; use zinc phosphide bait; scare devices at R3-R5
Harvest early if f>20% affected; assess maturity by black layer

Stages.Title: Harvest & Storage (105-120 DAS)
Stages.Description: Maturity indices, harvesting, drying and safe storage

Subsections.Heading: 9.1 Maturity Indices
Subsections.Text: Harvest at the correct moisture content is critical to avoid field losses and storage problems. Several indices help determine physiological maturity.

Table.Description: Abscission layer at kernel base turns black
Outer husk turns from green to straw-yellow
Press nail into dent area of grain

Table.Notes: Higher moisture = field losses; lower = shattering
Cobs harvested, husked, dried on cob
Depends on weather and layer thickness

Subsections.Heading: 9.3 Post-Harvest Drying Protocol

Table.Conditions Required: Spread in single layer, 3-4 hrs sunday/

Table.Remarks: Best for large quantities; seed quality preserved

Important Notes: Aflatoxin (Aspergillus flavus) grows rapidly in maize >14% moisture with >25°C temperature. Aflatoxin is carcinogenic; contaminated grain is rejected at all markets and export.
NEVER store grain > 14% moisture; test moisture with meter before storage.
Use perforated metal bins or reinforced plastic silos; add 3-4 neem leaves per bag.
Inspect stored grain every 30 days for insect damage, mould, or moisture rise.

Table.Recommendation: Hermetic/metal silo preferred; reinforced polypropylene bags for short-term
Aluminium phosphide (3 tablets / tonne) in sealed silo 72 hr exposure
Max 10 bags high; on pallets (15 cm off floor); 50 cm from wall
Every 30 days check moisture, insect frass, mould odour
Grade A: < 12% moisture, < 4% broken, < 1.5% foreign matter

Table.Action (THEN): Physiological maturity reached begin harvest planning
